raw_response:
I am getting old, so on just 2 mu I do not spread myself too thin. This year I will still plant maize on the whole plot. I have done this land for many years, and with a small area like mine, the safest thing is to keep to what I know. I have high education, so I do look at the crop more systematically than before, but in the end I still trust what has worked on my own field. Maize on this land can give a steady harvest if I plant on time, use a decent hybrid seed, put enough base fertilizer, and irrigate when the weather turns dry. Since I have well water, I am not completely at the mercy of the rain, but pumping costs money, so I will not water carelessly.

For fertilizer, I do not want to cut too much. If maize is short of nitrogen early, the loss is hard to recover later. But with only 2 mu, I also do not need to chase a very high yield by overspending. I will use a moderate rate, split between base and topdressing around the big flare stage, so the crop does not run short in the middle. Weed control I will handle once early, and insecticide only if I actually see pressure. Labor is mainly our own household labor. At my age I try to keep operations simple and timely rather than complicated.
